analysis.body:
Per the Census BTOS series, 16.0% of construction firms in NAICS 23 reported using AI in the last two weeks, up from 14.3% in the prior period. The series first asked the question in September 2023 and reports directly from firms on a fortnightly basis.

BuiltWorlds, which runs sector intelligence for buildings and infrastructure, concentrates its conference programming on AI and machine learning in the AEC/O industry. Its annual AI/ML Conference covers existing and emerging solutions and use cases across construction, building, and operation, along with implementation strategies and case studies. Its Buildings Conference emphasizes data centers and AI infrastructure. Across AGC, BuiltWorlds, and the proptech and contech trackers, the coverage points to computer-vision safety monitoring, BIM clash detection, and autonomous site scanning as tracked areas.

On the capital side, CREtech and MetaProp track venture flow across architecture, engineering, and construction technology alongside property tech, according to the sourced points. The excerpts do not report specific investment amounts or vendor concentration figures.

AGC, with over 27,000 member firms, surveys technology adoption and safety-technology compliance across US builders. Its survey data in the excerpt focuses on input costs, jobs, and project disruptions rather than AI adoption, so no additional AI-specific adoption figure is available from that source in this material. AGC's survey finds war and tariff impacts are disrupting projects and firms struggle to fill openings, but the excerpt does not tie these to AI deployment.

A reader deciding whether to deploy can take from the Census series that adoption is directly measured and has moved from 14.3% to 16.0%, and from BuiltWorlds that industry conference programming and case studies are available for implementation guidance. The material does not provide ROI evidence or regulatory posture.

https://www.agc.org/.brief: The Associated General Contractors of America describes a leadership course for project executives and a connected platform for heavy civil and infrastructure work. The group says it has over 27,000 member firms and provides services to address member needs and protect the public interest. According to an association survey, construction input costs rose 8.9% between August 2025 and August 2026, with war and tariff impacts disrupting projects. The association also reports contractors added 22,000 jobs in August and the construction unemployment rate hit a record low of 3.1%, while firms struggle to fill openings.

https://builtworlds.com/.brief: BuiltWorlds operates a membership network for buildings and infrastructure professionals. The organization hosts an annual Buildings Conference addressing innovation in building development, design, materials and systems, with particular focus on data centers and AI infrastructure. It also runs an annual AI/ML Conference exploring artificial intelligence and machine learning adoption across the architecture, engineering, construction and operations industry, covering implementation strategies, use cases, and lessons learned from companies deploying these technologies.
